access-control-entry.summary: An access control entry is one line on a guest list: it names a person or group and says what they may or may not do with something.

access-control-list.summary: An access control list is the full guest list for a door: every person or group and what each is allowed to do.

access-url.summary: An access URL is the address the search robot uses to reach a file or page when it collects information for search.

agent-action.summary: An action is something an agent can do for you rather than just say, such as sending an email or updating a record.

activity-feed.summary: An activity feed is like a news ticker of what the people, documents and topics you follow have been up to.

activity-flow.summary: An activity flow is a recipe being followed right now, one step after another.

activity-model.summary: An activity model is a ready-made routine, like a saved checklist of steps that you can reuse.

adaptive-card.summary: An Adaptive Card is a small, tidy panel with text, pictures and buttons that appears inside a chat, like a mini form.

after-event.summary: An after event is like a thank-you note sent once a job has finished.

agent.summary: An agent is an AI assistant that can do a job for you, such as answering questions about a policy or booking a room. You tell it what it should do, what it may know and what it may act on.

agent-365.summary: Agent 365 is a control panel for the AI agents an organisation uses, so someone can see them and keep them in check.

agent-builder.summary: Agent Builder is a quick way for people to create a simple agent for themselves or their team, mostly by describing what it should do.

agentic-ai.summary: Agentic AI is AI that can work through several steps to reach a goal, instead of just answering one question.

ai-builder.summary: AI Builder lets you add ready-made AI skills, such as reading text from a form, to apps and flows without needing data science knowledge.

ai-model.summary: An AI model is the trained "brain" inside an AI tool: it has learned patterns from lots of examples and uses them to produce an answer.

ai-safety.summary: AI safety is the set of habits and controls that stop an AI from causing harm or doing something unexpected.

ai-generated-content.summary: AI-generated content is anything an AI wrote or made for you: text, images, summaries, code and so on.

alert-subscription.summary: An alert subscription is a request that says: tell me by message whenever this thing changes.

alternate-account.summary: An alternate account is a second login for the same person, kept in a different place from their main one.

analyst.summary: Analyst is a ready-made Copilot helper that is good at working with numbers and data.

app-catalog.summary: The app catalog is a special SharePoint site where an organisation keeps the custom apps and extensions it has approved for its sites.

app-context.summary: App context is what Copilot can see about the thing you have open, such as the current document or email.

app-custom-action.summary: An app custom action is an extra button added to a site by an add-in, and it leads to more of that add-in's features.

app-part.summary: An app part is a window on a page that shows a small piece of an add-in.

app-web.summary: An app web is a small, separate SharePoint site created for a SharePoint-hosted add-in. It keeps the add-in's own files and lists apart from the site the add-in was installed on.

application-directory.summary: The application directory is a folder on a search server where its working files for search are kept.

application-session.summary: An application session is the time an application is open: it starts when you open it and ends when you close it.

audience-identifier.summary: An audience identifier is the unique name tag that tells SharePoint which audience you mean.

audience-rule.summary: An audience rule is the entry test for a club: if you meet the conditions, you are in.

authentication.summary: Authentication is proving who you are, like showing your pass at the entrance.

authorisation.summary: Authorisation decides what a person, Copilot or an agent is allowed to do once it is known who they are.

authoritative-page.summary: An authoritative page is a web page an administrator has marked as especially trustworthy, so search shows it nearer the top.

authority-level.summary: The authority level is a score that says how important a page is: 0 is the best.

autohost.summary: Autohost means the system puts the pieces of an add-in in the right places for you.

autopilot.summary: Autopilot is an AI helper that lives in your organisation and keeps working on its own between your requests, like a colleague with a standing job.

available-site-template.summary: An available site template is a layout you are allowed to pick when you create a new site.

azure-ai-foundry.summary: Azure AI Foundry is Microsoft's workshop in the cloud for building, testing and running AI applications and agents.

background-task.summary: A background task is work an agent keeps doing while you get on with something else.

backward-signing.summary: Backward signing describes how a handwritten signature runs: from left to right, or the other way round.

base-view-identifier.summary: The base view identifier is the number that picks out one saved way of looking at a list.

basic-page.summary: A basic page is a simple, plain page where one area can hold a piece of content.

bcs-solution-deployment.summary: BCS solution deployment is the process of getting a business-data solution from the server onto people's computers.

before-event.summary: A before event is a checkpoint that you must pass before the action can go ahead.

blank-site.summary: A blank site is an empty room: a new site with nothing set up in it yet.

bring-your-own-data.summary: Bring your own data means plugging your organisation's own information into an AI tool so its answers fit your business.

browser-context.summary: Browser context is the web page you are looking at, shared with an AI helper when you allow it.

business-chat.summary: Business Chat is an older name for the Copilot chat that could draw on your work information across apps.

business-connectivity-services.summary: Business Connectivity Services lets you bring data from other business systems into SharePoint and Office, so people can use it without leaving those tools.

business-data.summary: Business data is the information a company holds about its work: documents, emails, meetings, reports and records.

business-process.summary: A business process is a repeatable set of steps that gets a job done, like approving an expense.

business-process-flow.summary: A business process flow is a guided path through a record, like a checklist across the top of a form that tells you which step comes next.

business-system.summary: A business system is a company's main working software, such as customer, finance or HR systems.

caml.summary: CAML is a small XML language SharePoint uses to describe things like queries and views, a bit like a form with fixed boxes to fill in.

canvas-app.summary: A canvas app is an app you design screen by screen, like arranging a poster: you place buttons, forms and pictures exactly where you want them.

central-administration-site.summary: Central Administration is the control room of a SharePoint installation, where an administrator manages everything from one place.

chrome-control.summary: The chrome control draws the top bar of a page so that an add-in looks like it belongs inside SharePoint.

citation.summary: A citation is a pointer in an answer that shows where a statement came from, like a footnote.

cloud-flow.summary: A cloud flow is an automation that runs on Microsoft's servers, so it works even when your computer is off. Something starts it, such as a new email, a button press or a set time.

column-formatting.summary: Column formatting changes how a column looks in a list or library, for example showing a status as a coloured label, without writing a program.

communication-site.summary: A communication site is a SharePoint site for sharing information with many people, such as news, announcements and policies. It works like a company noticeboard or magazine: a few people write and many people read.

connector.summary: A connector is a ready-made plug that lets an app or automation talk to another service, such as Outlook or SharePoint, without writing code.

content-migration-package.summary: A content migration package is a box of files used to move content from one place to another.

content-placeholder.summary: A content placeholder is an empty spot on a page template that gets filled in with the real content.

content-type.summary: A content type is a reusable template that says what information belongs with a kind of item or document. For example, every "Contract" always carries a customer name and an end date, wherever it is stored.

content-type-group.summary: A content type group is a labelled shelf where similar content types are kept together.

content-type-identifier.summary: A content type identifier is the unique code that tells SharePoint exactly which content type you mean.

content-type-order.summary: Content type order is the sequence in which content types are listed, like the order of items on a menu.

content-type-resource-folder.summary: A content type resource folder is the drawer where a content type keeps its extra files.

content-type-schema.summary: A content type schema is the written blueprint of a content type: it spells out what the content type contains.

content-type-specific-view.summary: A content type specific view is a special way of showing a list for just one kind of item.

context.summary: Context is the background information given to an AI along with your question, so it can answer sensibly.

context-site.summary: The context site is simply the site you are working in at the moment of the request.

context-type.summary: A context type is a label that sorts an event handler into a group.

context-window.summary: The context window is how much an AI can keep in mind at once, like the size of its desk.

contextual-search-scope.summary: A contextual search scope narrows a search to the place you are in, such as one site or one list.

conversation-history.summary: Conversation history is the earlier part of a chat, which the AI reads so follow-up questions make sense.

copilot.summary: Copilot is Microsoft's name for the AI helpers built into its products, from Word and Teams to Windows and Azure.

copilot-control-system.summary: The Copilot Control System is the collection of admin tools for keeping Copilot and agents safe, managed and measured.

copilot-credits.summary: Copilot Credits are the units you spend when you use the more advanced, usage-billed parts of Copilot, a bit like top-up credit on a phone.

copilot-dashboard.summary: The Copilot Dashboard is a report that shows how much Copilot is being used and what difference it makes.

copilot-in-excel.summary: Copilot in Excel is an AI helper inside spreadsheets that can explain numbers and write formulas for you.

copilot-in-outlook.summary: Copilot in Outlook is an AI helper in your email that can draft replies and summarise long threads.

copilot-in-powerpoint.summary: Copilot in PowerPoint is an AI helper that can build and polish slide decks from your ideas or documents.

copilot-in-teams.summary: Copilot in Teams is an AI helper for meetings and chats that can summarise what was said and list actions.

copilot-in-word.summary: Copilot in Word is an AI writing helper that can draft, rewrite and summarise documents for you.

copilot-notebooks.summary: A Copilot Notebook is a place where you collect the files and notes for one topic so the AI can focus only on them.

copilot-pages.summary: Copilot Pages are shared pages where you keep the good bits of an AI chat and keep working on them with others.

copilot-studio.summary: Copilot Studio is where you build AI assistants, called agents, with little or no code. You describe what you want, give the agent knowledge and tools, then put it where people already work.

cowork.summary: Cowork is a Copilot mode where you describe a whole job and the AI plans it, does the steps across your tools and hands back a finished result.

crawl-log.summary: The crawl log is the diary of the search robot, noting where it succeeded and where it ran into problems.

crawl-queue.summary: The crawl queue is the to-do list of things the search robot will visit next.

crawled-property.summary: A crawled property is a piece of information the search robot finds about an item, like the author name on a book cover.

cross-domain-library.summary: The cross-domain library lets a page from one website talk to SharePoint on another site without being blocked.

custom-action.summary: A custom action is an extra menu item or ribbon button that a developer adds to a SharePoint page.

custom-engine-agent.summary: A custom engine agent is an assistant whose builders bring their own 'brain', the software and AI model that decide what to do, instead of using Copilot's.

customer-conversation-harness.summary: The Customer Conversation harness is the engine for agents that talk to your customers, not your staff.

data-boundary.summary: A data boundary is a line around where your organisation's data may be stored and processed, like a country border for information.

data-loss-prevention.summary: Data loss prevention is a set of rules that stop sensitive information being shared where it should not be.

data-minimisation.summary: Data minimisation means using only the information you really need for the job, and no more.

data-policy.summary: A data policy is a safety rule set by administrators that decides which services your apps and flows are allowed to connect with.

data-source.summary: A data source is any place an AI helper can look things up, such as SharePoint, email or a database.

data-view-web-part.summary: The Data View web part is a window on a page that shows the items of a list.

dataverse.summary: Dataverse is the place where Power Platform apps keep their data, in organised tables with built-in security. Think of it as a secure, well-labelled filing room.

dataverse-choice.summary: A choice is a column that lets people pick from a fixed list, like a drop-down for status: Open, In progress, Done.

dataverse-column.summary: A column is one detail you record about every row in a table, such as a customer's email address or an order's due date.

dataverse-row.summary: A row is a single entry in a table, such as one customer. It holds the values of every column for that one thing.

dataverse-table.summary: A Dataverse table is like a spreadsheet tab for one kind of thing, such as customers or orders. Each row is one customer, and each column is one detail about them.

declarative-agent.summary: A declarative agent is a version of Copilot that you set up for one purpose by writing instructions and choosing what it can look at and do. You do not build the thinking part yourself.

declarative-workflow-association.summary: A declarative workflow association connects a no-code workflow to the list or content type it should run on.

deep-research.summary: Deep research is when an AI spends longer digging through many sources and then writes a thorough report, instead of giving a quick reply.

default-list-view.summary: The default list view is the way a list looks when you open it without choosing anything special.

default-mobile-list-view.summary: The default mobile list view is the way a list looks on a phone or tablet when no other view is chosen.

default-search-scope.summary: The default search scope is the search area used automatically if nobody picks another one.

default-user-store.summary: The default user store is the first place that search looks to work out who belongs to which group.

deployment-system-object.summary: A deployment system object is a standard item that is automatically created along with a new site, such as its default home page.

descendant-content-type.summary: A descendant content type is a child that inherits from a parent, the way a family recipe is adapted for a new dish.

desktop-flow.summary: A desktop flow copies the clicks and typing a person would do on a computer, so a repetitive task, like copying details between two old programs, can run on its own.

document-library.summary: A document library is the place on a SharePoint site where you store, share and work on files together. It keeps earlier versions of each file and controls who can open or change it.

document-processing.summary: Document Processing for Microsoft 365 is a group of AI features that help read, sort and pull information out of documents stored in places such as SharePoint, so people do less manual filing.

draft.summary: A draft is a first version written by AI that you are meant to read and improve.

dynamic-grounding.summary: Dynamic grounding means the AI looks up the latest facts at the moment you ask, instead of using only what it already knew.

dynamic-rank.summary: Dynamic rank is how well a search result matches the words you typed, and it changes with every search.

ediscovery.summary: eDiscovery is how organisations find and collect electronic information for legal or investigation needs.

embedding.summary: An embedding is a list of numbers that captures the meaning of some text, so a computer can tell what is similar.

enterprise-data-protection.summary: Enterprise data protection is the set of safeguards that keeps your prompts and answers within your organisation's protections.

environment.summary: An environment is a separate workspace inside Power Platform. You might have one for testing and another for the real thing, so experiments never disturb live work.

evaluation.summary: Evaluation is testing an AI helper to see whether its answers are good enough.

everyday-ai-and-advanced-ai.summary: Microsoft splits Copilot into two kinds of work: everyday AI, which your licence already pays for, and advanced AI, which you pay for as you use it.

excluded-item.summary: An excluded item is something the search robot has been told to skip.

xai.summary: Explainable AI makes it easier to understand why an AI gave a particular answer.

extensibility.summary: Extensibility is the ability to add new abilities to Copilot, like adding attachments to a toolbox.

external-data.summary: External data is information kept outside Microsoft 365 that you may allow an AI helper to use.

extracted-definition.summary: An extracted definition is a sentence that the search system spotted and recognised as explaining a word.

extracted-term.summary: An extracted term is a word or phrase that search has picked out and has an explanation for.

fabric-iq.summary: Fabric IQ is a Microsoft layer that helps AI make sense of an organisation's analytical data.

farm-administrators-group.summary: The Farm Administrators group is the group of people trusted to look after all the servers that run SharePoint.

farm-solution.summary: A farm solution is an old-style package of custom code that an administrator installs on the servers that run SharePoint, so it affects every site on those servers.

feature-definition.summary: A feature definition is the instruction sheet for a feature, saying what it is called and what it can do.

feature-identifier.summary: A feature identifier is the unique ID number for a feature, like a serial number.

feature-property.summary: A feature property is a setting attached to a feature that has been switched on.

feature-scope.summary: The feature scope says how wide a feature reaches when it is turned on: one site, a whole group of sites, and so on.

federated-location.summary: A federated location is another place that can answer a search, so you can ask more than one library at once.

federated-location-definition.summary: A federated location definition is the instruction card that tells search how to ask another source and how to show its answers.

feedback.summary: Feedback is you telling the AI whether an answer was good or bad.

field-internal-name.summary: A field internal name is the fixed behind-the-scenes name of a column, which stays the same even if the visible title changes.

file-grounding.summary: File grounding means giving the AI a file to base its answer on, like handing a colleague the document and asking about it.

finance-agents.summary: Finance Agents are AI assistants made for finance teams, to help with finance tasks.

fine-tuning.summary: Fine-tuning is giving an AI model extra training so it gets better at a particular kind of task.

first-party-agents.summary: First-party agents are ready-made AI helpers that Microsoft supplies, so you hand them a job instead of building anything yourself.

model-driven-form.summary: A form is the screen where people create, read or update one row, like a paper form with a box for each detail.

forms-copilot.summary: Forms Copilot is AI help for making surveys and forms.

freshness.summary: Freshness is how up to date the information given to an AI is.

frontier.summary: Frontier is Microsoft's early-access club: an opt-in programme that lets your organisation try new Microsoft 365 features before they are officially released.

fsa-manager.summary: The FSA Manager is the supervisor service that runs the security side of FAST search.

fsa-worker.summary: The FSA worker is the helper service that works out what each person is allowed to see in search.

full-text-index-component.summary: A full-text index component is a set of files that works like the index at the back of a book, listing where each word is found.

general-availability.summary: General availability, or GA, means a feature is officially ready for everyone to use.

generation.summary: Generation is the AI writing its answer, one small piece at a time.

generative-ai.summary: Generative AI is AI that creates new things, such as text, images or code, from your instructions.

generative-answer.summary: A generative answer is a reply the AI composes on the spot, rather than picking a pre-written one.

generic-list.summary: A generic list is the plain, all-purpose kind of list: a simple table that you shape yourself.

governance.summary: Governance is the set of rules and responsibilities that decide how Copilot and agents may be created and used.

gpt.summary: GPT is a family of AI language models, and the name stands for generative pre-trained transformer.

graph-connector.summary: A Graph connector brings content from another system into Microsoft's search and AI, so people can find it in one place.

graph-grounding.summary: Graph grounding means the AI uses your work information, like files, mail and meetings, to answer you.

grounded-response.summary: A grounded response is an answer that was based on real sources, not just the AI's memory.

grounding.summary: Grounding means giving the AI the right facts to answer from, such as your documents, so it does not have to guess.

group-approval-document-identifier.summary: It is the unique reference number for a document that is going through a group sign-off.

guardrail.summary: A guardrail is a safety rail that keeps an AI from going where it should not.

hallucination.summary: A hallucination is when an AI states something that sounds confident but is wrong or made up.

hallucination-mitigation.summary: Hallucination mitigation is the set of tricks used to stop an AI from making things up.

handoff.summary: A handoff is when a job passes from one agent or step to another, or to a real person.

harmful-content.summary: Harmful content is material that could be unsafe, abusive, hateful or otherwise inappropriate.

harness.summary: A harness is the engine underneath an agent in Copilot Studio. The builder looks the same, but the engine decides how the agent behaves.

high-confidence-property.summary: A high confidence property is a piece of information that is a very strong clue that an item is exactly what someone is looking for.

high-confidence-result.summary: A high confidence result is a search answer that search is very sure about, shown prominently.

high-trust-app.summary: A high-trust app is an add-in that is trusted to say for itself who the user is.

home-site.summary: The home site is the one SharePoint site that acts as your organisation's front door, the landing page for the company intranet. It is the site people reach first from the SharePoint start page and from Viva Connections.

host-web.summary: The host web is the ordinary SharePoint site that an add-in is installed on. It is the place where the add-in's features show up.

hub-site.summary: A hub site links related SharePoint sites together so they feel like one connected area. Picture a department lobby with doors to several rooms: every room shares the same signs and style, and the news from all of them shows up in the lobby.

human-in-the-loop.summary: Human-in-the-loop means a person checks or approves what the AI does before it counts.

hybrid-search.summary: Hybrid search combines searching for exact words with searching by meaning.

identity.summary: Identity is the verified "who" behind an action, whether a person, a service or an agent.

image-generation.summary: Image generation is when AI draws a picture from a written description.

implicit-context.summary: Implicit context is the background an app supplies on its own, like the document you have open, without you attaching anything.

inference.summary: Inference is the moment a trained AI actually answers a new request.

information-barrier.summary: An information barrier is a wall between two groups of people that stops them communicating or sharing.

input.summary: Input is whatever you give the AI: your question, files, pictures or data.

intent.summary: Intent is what you are really trying to achieve, which the AI tries to work out from your words.

isolation.summary: Isolation keeps things apart so a problem or a breach in one place can't spread to others.

jailbreak.summary: A jailbreak is a trick that gets an AI to ignore its own safety rules.

job-automation.summary: Job automation is using AI and tools to take over the repeatable parts of someone's work.

json.summary: JSON is a simple, tidy text format for passing information between programs, a bit like a filled-in form.

just-in-time-access.summary: Just-in-time access gives someone powerful rights only when they need them, and only for a short while.

key-phrase.summary: A key phrase is a short phrase that captures an important idea in some content.

keyword-consumer.summary: A keyword consumer is a group of sites that all use the same set of search keywords and recommended answers.

keyword-search.summary: Keyword search finds things by matching the exact words you type.

keyword-synonym.summary: A keyword synonym is another way of saying the same search word, such as "car" for "automobile".

knowledge-graph.summary: A knowledge graph is a map of things and how they relate, such as people, projects and documents.

knowledge-source.summary: Knowledge is what an agent is allowed to read in order to answer you, such as a set of documents, a website or a database.

kql.summary: KQL is an abbreviation for two different query languages, so check which one is meant.

language-auto-detection.summary: Language auto-detection means the system works out for itself which language a document is written in.

large-language-model.summary: A large language model, or LLM, is a computer program trained on huge amounts of text so it can predict and write language. That is what lets AI assistants hold a conversation.

latency.summary: Latency is how long you wait between asking and getting the answer.

least-privilege.summary: Least privilege means giving a person or app only the rights needed to do its job, and nothing extra.

licence.summary: A licence is what you pay for or are assigned that unlocks a feature for you.

lifecycle-management.summary: Lifecycle management is looking after an agent from the first idea until it is switched off.

line-of-business-data.summary: Line-of-business data is the information kept in a company's main operational systems, such as sales, finance or support.

list-folder.summary: A list folder is a folder inside a list that keeps related items together.

list-form.summary: A list form is the page where you fill in or look at the details of one list item.

list-form-web-part.summary: The List Form web part is the building block that draws a list form on a page.

list-identifier.summary: A list identifier is the unique code of a list, so that it can never be confused with another list.

list-item-attachment.summary: A list item attachment is a file stuck onto a list item, like a document paper-clipped to a form.

list-item-identifier.summary: A list item identifier is the number that picks out one item in a list.

list-server-template.summary: A list server template value tells SharePoint which kind of list blueprint was used.

list-template.summary: A list template is a saved pattern for a list, so you can create more lists exactly like it.

list-template-identifier.summary: A list template identifier is the unique code of a list template.

list-view-page.summary: A list view page is a page whose main job is to show a list.

list-view-threshold.summary: The list view threshold is a safety limit that stops one view or search from working through too many items at once, so a big list does not slow everyone down.

list-view-web-part.summary: The List View web part is the reusable block that shows a list's items as a table on a page.

log.summary: A log is a written record of what happened, kept so someone can look back later.

log-level.summary: A log level is a dial that sets how much detail gets written to a log.

loop-component.summary: A Loop component is a small live block of content, such as a list or table, that stays in sync wherever it is shared.

managed-keyword.summary: A managed keyword is a tag you can add to an item so that it is easy to find and group later.

meeting-recap.summary: A meeting recap is a summary of a meeting: key points, decisions and who is doing what.

member-group.summary: A member group is a group of people that the profile service tracks, not the same as the site group called Members.

member-group-source.summary: The member group source says where a group of people comes from, such as a particular company directory.

members-group.summary: The Members group is the standard group for the people who do the day-to-day work on a site.

membership-group-record-identifier.summary: It is the unique ID for one record about a group membership.

memory.summary: Memory lets an AI remember useful things about you or your work between chats.

metadata.summary: Metadata is the "label on the box": facts about a file like its author, date and type.

metadata-index.summary: The metadata index is a catalogue, stored on a database server, of the details that go with each item.

metadata-schema.summary: A metadata schema is the rule sheet that says what facts are kept about an item.

microsoft-365-archiving.summary: Microsoft 365 Archiving lets an organisation move SharePoint sites that nobody uses any more to cheaper storage, while keeping their content so it can be brought back later.

microsoft-365-backup.summary: Microsoft 365 Backup keeps backup copies of an organisation's SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content, so it can be put back quickly after it is lost or damaged.

microsoft-365-copilot-chat.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) is the chat assistant for work: you type a question and get an answer, with your organisation's data protections in place.

microsoft-365-copilot.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 apps such as Word, Outlook and Teams. You ask it in everyday language and it helps you write, summarise and find things, using your own work information.

microsoft-365-copilot-app.summary: The Microsoft 365 Copilot app is the home screen for Microsoft 365 on the web and your devices, where you start work, find your files and open Copilot.

appsource.summary: AppSource is Microsoft's online marketplace for ready-made business apps and add-ons, including ones for SharePoint, from Microsoft and other companies.

microsoft-copilot-harness.summary: The Microsoft Copilot harness is the engine for agents that work through a goal on their own, step by step. It used to be called the GitHub Copilot harness, and the name changed on 28 October 2026.

microsoft-entra-id.summary: Microsoft Entra ID is the service that knows who your people are and signs them in.

microsoft-graph.summary: Microsoft Graph is the connection point to the information in your Microsoft 365 account, such as your files, mail, meetings and people. It is how apps ask for that information in a controlled way.

microsoft-iq.summary: Microsoft IQ is Microsoft's overall approach to giving agents knowledge of your work, data and context.

microsoft-purview.summary: Microsoft Purview is the set of tools for protecting data and meeting compliance rules.

microsoft-scout.summary: Microsoft Scout is a name you will meet in two places: the original name of Autopilot, and the name of a desktop app that works across your files and apps.

microsoft-search.summary: Microsoft Search is the search tool across Microsoft 365 for finding people, files, sites and messages.

model-context-protocol.summary: MCP is a common plug standard that lets AI tools connect to other tools and data in the same way.

model-driven-app.summary: A model-driven app is built around your data: you decide what information you keep and the app builds the screens for it. It is like starting from a filing system rather than a blank page.

moderated-object.summary: A moderated object is something that must be checked by a reviewer before others can see it.

moderation.summary: Moderation is checking what goes into and comes out of an AI so unsafe content is caught.

moderation-status.summary: Moderation status is the label that says whether an item has been approved yet.

multimodal-ai.summary: Multimodal AI can handle more than one kind of information, such as text, pictures and sound.

multivalue-property.summary: A multivalue property is a field that can hold more than one value, like a contact with several phone numbers.

named-entity-recognition.summary: Named entity recognition finds the names of people, places, companies, dates and products in text.

natural-language.summary: Natural language is ordinary human language, the way you talk or write.

natural-language-processing.summary: Natural language processing is the field of teaching computers to understand and produce human language.

navigation-structure.summary: A navigation structure is the signposting of a site: the links that lead you between its parts.

neural-network.summary: A neural network is a computer structure loosely inspired by the brain that learns patterns from examples.

new-form.summary: A new form is the page you fill in to add a new item to a list.

news-post.summary: A news post is a page that shares an announcement or a story with the people who follow a site. It appears in news feeds and on the SharePoint start page.

no-code-agent.summary: A no-code agent is an AI helper you set up by describing it, without writing programs.

non-deterministic-output.summary: Non-deterministic output means asking the same question twice can give two different, equally reasonable answers.

notification.summary: A notification is a ping telling you something finished or needs you.

office-sharepoint-server-search-service.summary: This is the search engine service of the older Office SharePoint Server product.

onedrive.summary: OneDrive is the personal online storage that comes with a work or school Microsoft 365 account. It is your own private folder in the cloud, and you choose what to share with others.

open-item-permission.summary: Open Item permission is the right to open and read a whole file.

open-web-permission.summary: Open web permission is the right to open a site, needed when you export or import it.

openai-model.summary: An OpenAI model is an AI model made by the company OpenAI.

operator-account.summary: The operator account is the login of the person running a content import.

orchestration.summary: Orchestration is the conductor's job: coordinating the model, the instructions, the lookups and the tools so a task gets done.

orchestrator.summary: The orchestrator is the agent's project manager: it decides which information to look up and which tools to use, and in what order, to answer you.

organisational-context.summary: Organisational context is what the AI knows about how your organisation works: roles, relationships, files and activity.

organisational-data.summary: Organisational data is information your organisation owns or manages.

organisational-search.summary: Organisational search finds things across your workplace: people, documents, messages and sites.

organization-identifier.summary: An organization identifier is the unique number that stands for one organisation.

orphaned-object.summary: An orphaned object is something left behind that has lost its parent, like a file in a folder that no longer exists.

output.summary: Output is what the AI gives back: text, a decision, a recommendation or an action.

oversight.summary: Oversight is people keeping an eye on AI systems so they stay useful, safe and on track.

paged-view.summary: A paged view shows a long list a page at a time instead of all at once.

parent-farm.summary: A parent farm is the main farm that gathers information from another farm and answers questions about it.

parent-list.summary: A parent list is the list that holds a given item or folder.

performancepoint-data-connections-librar.summary: This is a special library that keeps the data connections for PerformancePoint dashboards.

permission-trimming.summary: Permission trimming means search and AI only show you what you already have the right to see.

personal-site.summary: A personal site is a person's own space on SharePoint, used for their own work.

personalisation.summary: Personalisation is the AI adapting its answers to you: your role, preferences and work habits.

planner-agent.summary: The Planner Agent is an AI assistant that helps with project and plan management.

plugin.summary: A plugin is an older name for an add-on that gives an AI assistant extra abilities.

policy.summary: A policy is a rule that says what is and isn't allowed.

portal-content.summary: Portal content is the main collection of what search has gathered, with its sources and settings.

power-apps.summary: Power Apps lets people build business apps without being professional programmers, by placing things on a screen and describing behaviour with simple formulas.

power-automate.summary: Power Automate lets you set up a chain of steps that runs by itself, such as saving email attachments to a folder or asking a manager to approve a request.

power-bi.summary: Power BI turns data into charts and reports so people can see what is happening in the business at a glance.

power-fx.summary: Power Fx is the simple formula language used in Power Apps. If you have written a formula in Excel, it will look familiar.

power-pages.summary: Power Pages is for building websites that people outside your organisation can use, such as a customer portal or a sign-up page, without writing a website from scratch.

power-platform.summary: Power Platform is Microsoft's family of low-code tools for building apps, automating work, making websites and analysing data. Think of it as a workshop with a different tool for each job, all sharing the same shelves of data.

power-platform-admin-center.summary: The Power Platform admin center is the control room where administrators look after environments, settings and policies.

preview.summary: Preview means a feature is available early and may still change.

principal-aliasing.summary: Principal aliasing is a way of saying "this person in one list is the same as that person in another".

privacy-level.summary: The privacy level decides who is allowed to see your personal details on your profile.

prompt.summary: A prompt is what you type or send to an AI to tell it what you want. A clearer prompt usually gets a better answer.

prompt-chaining.summary: Prompt chaining splits a big job into a series of smaller asks, each building on the last.

prompt-engineering.summary: Prompt engineering is the skill of asking the AI in a clear way so the answer is useful.

prompt-gallery.summary: A prompt gallery is a library of ready-made questions to try with Copilot.

prompt-injection.summary: Prompt injection is sneaking hidden instructions into content so the AI follows the attacker's orders.

protected-material.summary: Protected material is content covered by copyright or similar protection.

provisioned.summary: Provisioned means that something has been set up and made ready for use.

public-filter.summary: The public filter lets search show items that everyone is allowed to see.

publish-to-server.summary: Publish to server means saving a document, or part of one, to a web server.

published-version.summary: A published version is the approved copy that everyone can see.

publishing-level.summary: The publishing level is a number that says where a version is in the publishing process.

publishing-page.summary: A publishing page is a page built by pouring content into a ready-made layout.

qa.summary: Q&A is asking a question and getting an answer.

query.summary: A query is a request for information sent to a search or data service.

query-expansion.summary: Query expansion adds related words to a search so it finds more relevant things.

query-independent-rank.summary: Query independent rank is a score for how important an item is, whatever you search for.

query-table.summary: A query table is a spreadsheet-like table filled with data from another system.

quick-action.summary: A quick action is a one-click shortcut for a common Copilot task.

quota.summary: A quota is a limit on how much you can use a service.

ranking-parameter.summary: A ranking parameter is a dial that influences which items appear higher in search results.

reasoning.summary: Reasoning is the AI working out an answer step by step rather than blurting it out.

recommendation.summary: A recommendation is a suggestion made by AI.

recycle-bin.summary: The Recycle Bin is where deleted SharePoint files and items wait before they are gone for good. You can restore your own deleted items from the site's Recycle Bin. If they are removed from there, they move to a second-stage bin that only site collection administrators can restore from.

red-teaming.summary: Red teaming is deliberately trying to break an AI system to find its weak spots.

researcher.summary: Researcher is a ready-made Copilot helper for digging into a topic across many sources.

response.summary: A response is the reply you get back from Copilot or an agent.

responsible-ai.summary: Responsible AI means building and using AI fairly, safely and transparently, with someone accountable.

retention.summary: Retention is the rule for how long content is kept before it is deleted or reviewed.

retrieval.summary: Retrieval is the AI looking up relevant information before it answers.

risk-management.summary: Risk management is spotting what could go wrong with AI and deciding what to do about it.

role-identifier.summary: A role identifier is the unique number of a role, such as a permission level, within a site.

role-type.summary: A role type is one of the standard permission sets that come ready-made.

role-based-access-control.summary: Role-based access control gives people rights according to their job role instead of one by one.

root-document.summary: A root document is a file that sits at the very top level of a site, not inside a folder.

safe-completion.summary: Safe completion is an AI staying helpful while steering clear of unsafe requests.

scheduled.summary: Scheduled means an item has a set date and time for going live or being taken down.

schema-version.summary: The schema version is the edition number of the rule sheet that a deployment package follows.

search-application.summary: A search application is one self-contained set of search settings.

search-catalog.summary: The search catalog is the big collection of facts that search gathered, used to answer your questions.

search-database.summary: The search database is where search keeps its notes, in a database.

search-query-log.summary: The search query log is a record of what people searched for and when.

search-scope-consumer.summary: A search scope consumer is a site collection that uses a particular menu of search areas.

search-scope-display-group.summary: A search scope display group is a menu that lists the search areas people can choose from.

search-scope-index.summary: The search scope index is a speed-up for searches that are limited to a scope.

search-scope-rule.summary: A search scope rule decides what is included in a search area.

search-service-account.summary: The search service account is the login the search service runs under.

search-shared-application-object.summary: This is the object that holds the settings shared by a search application.

security-role.summary: A security role is a set of permissions, like a job badge that says which doors a person can open and what they can do inside.

semantic-index.summary: A semantic index is a search catalogue that understands meaning, not just words.

semantic-search.summary: Semantic search finds results by meaning and intent, not just matching words.

sensitivity-label.summary: A sensitivity label is a tag on a file saying how confidential it is and how it must be handled.

server-to-server-protocol.summary: The server-to-server protocol is how two servers prove who they are to each other.

session.summary: A session is one stretch of interaction with Copilot or an agent.

shadow-ai.summary: Shadow AI is AI tools people use at work without the organisation's approval or knowledge.

shared-documents-library.summary: The Shared Documents library is the ready-made folder for files that comes with a new team site.

shared-view.summary: A shared view is a way of looking at a list that everyone allowed to see it can use.

sharepoint-add-in.summary: SharePoint Add-ins are an older way to give SharePoint sites extra features, using small apps installed on a site. In SharePoint Online they stopped working on 2 April 2026, and newer extras are built with the SharePoint Framework instead.

spfx.summary: The SharePoint Framework, or SPFx, is the modern way for developers to build custom extras for SharePoint, such as new page building blocks, that run safely inside SharePoint pages.

sharepoint-groups.summary: SharePoint groups are the permission buckets of a site. Owners can do everything, Members can add and edit, and Visitors can only read.

sharepoint-list.summary: A SharePoint list is a table of information, such as tasks, issues, contacts or equipment, that everyone with access can view and update. Each row is an item and each column holds one kind of detail.

sharepoint-online.summary: SharePoint Online is the cloud version of SharePoint that comes with Microsoft 365. Microsoft runs the servers for you, so there is nothing to install or look after.

sharepoint-search-sql-syntax.summary: This is a way to write a search question in the style of a database query.

sharepoint-server.summary: SharePoint Server is the version of SharePoint that an organisation installs and runs on its own servers, instead of using Microsoft's cloud.

sharepoint-site.summary: A SharePoint site is a website inside Microsoft 365 where a team or organisation keeps its files, news, lists and pages in one place. Think of it as a shared online room: it has its own address, its own furniture (files and lists) and its own guest list (who may come in).

sharing-link.summary: A sharing link is a web address you create to give someone access to a file or folder in SharePoint or OneDrive. The type of link decides who can use it.

single-sign-on.summary: Single sign-on lets you sign in once and use many apps.

single-sign-on-ticket.summary: A single sign-on ticket is like a stamped pass, so you don't have to show your ID again at every door.

site-collection.summary: A site collection is a group of SharePoint sites that share one top-level site and one set of settings. Think of a building: the building has shared rules and storage, and each room is a site inside it.

site-collection-administrator.summary: A site collection administrator is the person who is in charge of a whole group of sites.

site-collection-flag.summary: A site collection flag is a set of on-off switches that describe a whole group of sites.

site-collection-identifier.summary: A site collection identifier is the unique code of a site collection.

site-collection-quota.summary: A site collection quota is a size limit that stops a group of sites growing without end.

site-column.summary: A site column is a reusable piece of information, such as "Project owner" or "Due date", that you define once and can then use in many lists and libraries on a site.

site-definition.summary: A site definition is a family of blueprints for sites.

site-definition-configuration.summary: A site definition configuration is one complete blueprint for a type of site.

site-definition-version.summary: The site definition version is the edition number of a site blueprint.

site-flag.summary: A site flag is a set of on-off switches that describe one site.

site-identifier.summary: A site identifier is the unique code of a single site.

model-driven-site-map.summary: The site map is the menu of a model-driven app: it decides which sections and pages people can click in the navigation.

site-membership.summary: Site membership means you belong to a site and have been given a set of rights on it.

site-page.summary: A site page is a web page inside a SharePoint site. You build it by adding sections and blocks of content, such as text, images and lists.

site-property.summary: A site property is a named fact about a site, such as its title or default language.

site-solution.summary: A site solution is a ready-to-install package of extras that can be switched on for individual sites.

site-template.summary: A site template is a saved starting point for new sites.

skill.summary: A skill is a reusable ability you can hand to an agent, like giving a helper a new instruction card.

solution.summary: A solution is a box that you pack your apps and flows into so you can carry them from one environment to another.

source.summary: A source is the document, page or record that an answer was based on.

speech-to-text.summary: Speech-to-text turns spoken words into written text.

standard-harness.summary: The standard harness is the engine for agents that follow the conversation paths and rules that you write, so they behave predictably.

start-address.summary: A start address is the web address where the search robot begins.

static-rank.summary: Static rank is how important search thinks an item is, independent of what you typed.

summarisation.summary: Summarisation is shortening a long thing into its main points.

supervised-learning.summary: Supervised learning is teaching a model with examples that come with the right answers.

synthetic-data.summary: Synthetic data is made-up data that looks like the real thing.

system-prompt.summary: A system prompt is the hidden set of rules an AI app gives the model before your question.

task.summary: A task is one job you ask Copilot or an agent to do, from a quick summary to a whole process.

task-orchestration.summary: Task orchestration is arranging several steps, tools and data lookups in the right order to reach a bigger goal.

team-site.summary: A team site is a SharePoint site built for people who work together on a project or in a department. It is the team's shared workspace for files, tasks and news, where everyone on the team can add and edit.

temperature.summary: Temperature is a dial for how adventurous an AI's wording is.

tenant.summary: A tenant is your organisation's own private space in Microsoft's cloud.

tenant-data.summary: Tenant data is everything stored in your organisation's Microsoft cloud tenant.

term-store.summary: The term store is a central list of agreed words, such as department names or product categories. People pick from it when they tag files, so everyone tags things the same way.

token.summary: A token is a small chunk of text, roughly a short word or part of one, that an AI reads and writes.

tool-calling.summary: Tool calling is when an AI decides to use a tool, like a calculator or a search, to get something done.

topic.summary: A topic is one conversation an agent knows how to have, such as 'reset my password' or 'opening hours'.

trace.summary: A trace is a step-by-step record of how an agent handled a request.

transcript.summary: A transcript is a written copy of what was said in a conversation or meeting.

trusted-authentication.summary: Trusted authentication lets one account act on behalf of the person who is currently signed in.

trusted-subsystem.summary: A trusted subsystem is a pair of servers that trust each other to do privileged jobs.

ui-culture.summary: The UI culture is the language that a screen uses to talk to you.

unified-audit-log.summary: The unified audit log is a central record of activity across Microsoft services.

unstructured-data.summary: Unstructured data is information that doesn't fit neat rows and columns, like documents, emails and chats.

upload.summary: Uploading is giving a file straight to the AI.

usage-report.summary: A usage report shows how much Copilot and agents are used.

usage-based-billing.summary: Usage-based billing means you pay for what you use rather than a flat fee.

user-context.summary: User context is what is known about the person asking: who they are, their role, files and activity.

user-display-name.summary: A user display name is the name a person prefers to be shown as.

user-grounding.summary: User grounding is the AI using information about you to make an answer fit your work.

user-permissions.summary: User permissions are the access rights a person has.

user-profile-change-entry-log.summary: The user profile change entry log is the diary of every change made to profiles.

user-profile-change-event.summary: A user profile change event is the moment when something on a profile changes.

user-profile-import.summary: A user profile import is the process of bringing people's details in from the company directory.

user-profile-record-identifier.summary: It is the unique number of one profile record.

user-profile-store.summary: The user profile store is the database that keeps everyone's profile details.

user-search-security-filter.summary: The user search security filter is a list of what each person may see, applied to search results so that people never see things they should not.

user-store.summary: A user store is a list of people, groups and their rights that belongs to another security system.

variable.summary: A variable is a named box that holds a value for later, such as what the user typed.

vector.summary: A vector is a list of numbers that stands for the meaning of something.

vector-database.summary: A vector database stores those number lists so similar things can be found quickly.

vector-search.summary: Vector search finds content whose meaning is close to your question.

verification.summary: Verification is checking an AI answer against something reliable before you use it.

version-history.summary: Version history keeps earlier copies of a file or list item every time it is saved, so you can look back at changes or bring an older version back.

model-driven-view.summary: A view is a saved way of looking at a list of rows, with chosen columns and filters, like a filtered spreadsheet you can reopen.

visible-scope.summary: A visible scope is a search area that people can actually see and choose.

visitors-group.summary: The Visitors group is the standard group for people who may look but not change things.

viva-engage.summary: Viva Engage is Microsoft's social network for organisations, where people share updates and join communities.

viva-insights.summary: Viva Insights is Microsoft's service about how people work, including collaboration patterns and wellbeing.

voice-input.summary: Voice input means speaking your request instead of typing.

web-application-identifier.summary: A web application identifier is the unique code of a web application.

web-control.summary: A web control is a reusable building block on the server that draws part of a page.

web-data.summary: Web data is information from public web pages given to the AI as context.

web-discussion-comment.summary: A web discussion comment is a single note added to a web discussion.

web-grounding.summary: Web grounding lets the AI check the internet for current information when answering.

web-part.summary: A web part is a building block you place on a SharePoint page, such as a text box, an image gallery, a news feed or a list of documents. You build a page by stacking web parts.

web-part-cache.summary: The web part cache is a quick-reference list that web parts use to look up information fast.

web-part-chrome-state.summary: The chrome state says whether a web part is shown open or collapsed.

web-part-connection.summary: A web part connection is a link between two web parts so one can pass data to the other.

web-part-identifier.summary: A web part identifier is the unique code of one web part on a page.

web-part-property.summary: A web part property is a setting that changes how a web part behaves.

web-part-type-identifier.summary: A web part type identifier is the unique code of a kind of web part.

web-part-zone-identifier.summary: It is the name tag of an area on a page where web parts can be placed.

web-part-zone-index.summary: The zone index sets the order of web parts in the same area.

web-proxy.summary: The web proxy is a go-between that lets SharePoint pass a request on to another service.

web-search.summary: Web search is looking things up on the internet.

web-service-method.summary: A web service method is an action that a service offers, which other programs can ask for.

whiteboard-copilot.summary: Whiteboard Copilot is AI help for brainstorming on a shared whiteboard.

work-iq.summary: Work IQ is Microsoft's way of giving Copilot and agents an understanding of how your work happens.

work-iq-api.summary: The Work IQ API lets approved apps and agents use Work IQ.

work-iq-data-layer.summary: The data layer is the part of Work IQ that gathers signals from files, email, meetings and chats.

work-iq-inference-layer.summary: The inference layer is where models, skills and tools work together on Work IQ context.

work-iq-mcp.summary: Work IQ MCP is a way for agents to use Work IQ through the standard MCP plug.

work-iq-memory-layer.summary: The memory layer builds lasting knowledge of work patterns and priorities.

work-item-process.summary: A work item process is the program that actually carries out a piece of queued work.

work-item-type-identifier.summary: It is the unique code for a kind of work item.

workflow.summary: A workflow is a defined series of steps that moves work from start to finish.

workflow-agent.summary: A workflow agent carries out or coordinates the steps of a process, instead of only chatting.

workflow-association.summary: A workflow association attaches a workflow to a list or a type of item so that it can run.

workflow-configuration-file.summary: The workflow configuration file is the settings sheet that pulls a workflow's parts together.

workflow-history-item.summary: A workflow history item is one entry in the story of what a workflow has done.

workflow-history-list.summary: The workflow history list is the logbook of a business process.

workflow-identifier.summary: A workflow identifier is the unique code of a workflow.

workflow-markup-file.summary: The workflow markup file is the written description of what a workflow does.

workflow-task.summary: A workflow task is one job in the chain of a business process.

workflow-task-list.summary: The workflow task list is the to-do list of a business process.

workplace-intelligence.summary: Workplace intelligence is understanding drawn from your organisation's data, relationships and activity.

workspace.summary: A workspace is a lasting area that groups the content, tools and activity for one piece of work.

xlsx-file.summary: An XLSX file is a standard Excel spreadsheet file.

xml.summary: XML is a text format that stores information inside labelled tags.

yaml.summary: YAML is a readable text format often used for settings.

zero-trust.summary: Zero Trust means never assuming anyone is safe just because they are on the company network.

zero-based-index.summary: A zero-based index starts counting at 0, not 1, the way a ruler starts at zero.

zero-shot-classification.summary: Zero-shot classification sorts items into categories without having been shown examples of those categories.

zero-shot-learning.summary: Zero-shot learning is when a model handles a task it was not specifically trained on.

zero-shot-prompting.summary: Zero-shot prompting is asking the AI to do something with instructions only, without showing examples.
